To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the crosslink density distribution in the spherical microgels can be controlled by the use of hydroxyl functional crosslinking agents.
we have synthesized thermosensitive micro-gels with quadratic cross-linking density distribution by using relatively hydro-philic crosslinkers with hydroxyl functionalities.
hydrophilic crosslinked N-isopropyleacrylamide based microgels can be obtained by using hydroxilated crosslinking agents and the hydrodynamic diameters of these microgels are temperature dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of hydroxyl functional microgels with different crosslinking density distributions.
the synthesis of hydroxyl functional thermosensitive microspheres with quadratic crosslink density distribution.
the synthesis of thermoresponsive microgels with hydroxyl functional groups on their surfaces and the determination of the crosslink density profile in these particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hydroxyl functionality of the crosslinker is the most important factor in the formation of the fringes and the quadratic crosslinking agent density distribution in the microgels.

the hydrodynamic size of microgels in the fully swollen and shrunken form decreased in the order of GDMA, PEPTA, PETA, and the volume phase transition of microgels was more pronounced with the increase of hydrophilicity of crosslinking agent.
the use of hydroxyl functional crosslinking agents led to the formation microgels with hydroxyl functional fringes on the particle surface and a quadratic crosslinking distribution in the particle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hydrophilic cross-linking agents can be used in the synthesis of thermoresponsive microgels with long flexible chains on the surface.

the use of hydroxyl functional crosslinking agents led to the formation thermosensitive micro-gels with quadratic cross linking density distribution and flexible hydroxyl functional fringes on the particle surface.

hydrophilic crosslinks can be utilized in the dispersion polymerizations of thermosensitive polymers to obtain the microgels with chemically derivatized surface and the crosslinking agents can be chosen to tune the surface properties and the swelling behavior of the thermosensitive particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crosslinker type has a significant effect on the swelling behavior of the microgels.
the crosslinker hydrophobicity is an important factor to be considered in the dispersion polymerizations of NIPA to synthesize microgels with the quadratic crosslinking distribution.
the hydroxyl functionalization of microgels can be performed by using a single-stage dispersion copolymerization of NIPA and a crosslinking agent with hydroxyl groups.
